title: “Householder, suppose a person borrows goods — luxurious vehicles, fine jewelry and ornaments — and with those borrowed goods he goes through the market, being…
content: “Householder, suppose a person borrows goods — luxurious vehicles, fine jewelry and ornaments — and with those borrowed goods he goes through the market, being honored and surrounded by many people. The crowd sees him and says: ‘This person is truly wealthy, and the wealthy enjoy such things.’ But wherever the owners see him, they take back their possessions. What do you think, householder? Is that person’s disguise then ended?” “Yes, venerable sir. Why is that? Because the owners take back their possessions.” … “So too, householder, a noble disciple reflects: ‘The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are like borrowed goods — of much suffering, much despair, and the peril is even greater.’ Having seen this as it actually is with perfect wisdom … he cultivates such equanimity.”

title: “Monks, dwell contemplating foulness in the body. Establish well mindfulness of breathing, setting mindfulness before you, inwardly directed. Dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned things.…
content:
“Monks, dwell contemplating foulness in the body. Establish well mindfulness of breathing, setting mindfulness before you, inwardly directed. Dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned things. For one dwelling contemplating foulness in the body, the underlying tendency to lust for the beautiful is abandoned. For one who has well-established mindfulness of breathing, setting mindfulness before you, inwardly directed, there are no externally directed, harmful thoughts. For one dwelling contemplating impermanence in all conditioned things, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.

Contemplating foulness in the body,
Mindful of in-breath and out-breath,
Calming all conditioned things,
Ever ardent, right in view —

That monk who sees rightly,
From that, being thus liberated,
Perfects direct knowledge,
Is at peace, truly stilled —
That sage has certainly crossed beyond all yokes.”

title: “‘I will dwell contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world.’ Thus, monk, you should…
content: “‘I will dwell contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world.’ Thus, monk, you should train. Monk, when this concentration of yours is developed and cultivated in this way, then, monk, you should develop this concentration with initial and sustained thought; you should develop it without initial thought but with sustained thought; you should develop it without initial and sustained thought; you should develop it with rapture; you should develop it without rapture; you should develop it accompanied by pleasure; you should develop it accompanied by equanimity. Monk, when this concentration of yours is developed and cultivated in this way, then, monk, wherever you go, you will go at ease; wherever you stand, you will stand at ease; wherever you sit, you will sit at ease; wherever you lie down, you will lie down at ease.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who attends unwisely, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”

title: Elder Abhaya (2): “Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost — Attending to a pleasing sign, The mind feels infatuation, Clinging to the perception remains. The…
content:
Elder Abhaya (2):
“Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost —
Attending to a pleasing sign,
The mind feels infatuation,
Clinging to the perception remains.
The defilements increase,
Leading to the root of existence.”

title: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple dwells with aroused energy, abandoning unwholesome states and acquiring wholesome states, steadfast, vigorous, not shirking the burden of wholesome states.…
content: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple dwells with aroused energy, abandoning unwholesome states and acquiring wholesome states, steadfast, vigorous, not shirking the burden of wholesome states. He has mindfulness, endowed with supreme mindfulness and discernment, recollecting and recalling what was done and said long ago. He has wisdom, endowed with wisdom regarding arising and passing away, noble and penetrating, leading to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with noble qualities.”

title: Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: As if struck by a sword, As if…
content:
Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning lust for sensual pleasures.

(The Blessed One):
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning identity view.

title: Venerable Kappa: “For those standing in the middle of the flood, In the terrifying current of existence, Overcome by old age and death — Tell…
content:
Venerable Kappa:
“For those standing in the middle of the flood,
In the terrifying current of existence,
Overcome by old age and death —
Tell me, sir, an island,
That there may be no further suffering.”

The Blessed One replied to Kappa:
“For those standing in the middle of the flood,
In the terrifying current of existence,
Overcome by old age and death —
I will tell you, Kappa, an island.

This island is unique —
Possessing nothing, not clinging —
I call it Nibbāna,
The destruction of old age and death.

Knowing this, mindful,
Attaining Nibbāna in this very life,
They do not come into Māra’s power,
Do not become servants of Māra.”

title: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds…
content: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds and persist; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of impermanence; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of not-self; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of foulness; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of peril; having known the world’s even and uneven, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s arising and passing away, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s origination and cessation, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of abandoning; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of dispassion; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of cessation.’ Thus, monks, you should train.”

title: “Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for…
content: “Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for the sake of eradicating defilements in the future. Cunda, I teach the Dhamma both for preventing defilements in the present life and for eradicating defilements in the future.”
